subject: Re: POC deep-dive sprint — coordination & realignment
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@brightpath.ai>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: POC deep-dive sprint — proposed kickoff blocks and hands-on windows

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Great to be moving forward with BrightPath for the inference pilot. We want the kickoff to be high-velocity but also respectful of your team's time zones. Attached is a short agenda and a first-pass runbook for the hands-on sessions.

Goal: align on three focused deep-dive slots (prompt review + routing config + 2x load tests) across US / EU / APAC so your engineers can attend at least one live block and we can rotate the heavy tests to minimize impact.

Proposed schedule (all times listed in local region examples — we will send calendar invites in your preferred timezone):
- Day 1: 14:00 US-ET / 19:00 EU (short overlap) — Quick architecture & routing review (45m) + open Q&A
- Day 2: 08:30 EU / 20:30 APAC — Prompt workshop (60m) + prompt set validation run
- Day 3: 23:00 US-PT / 11:00 APAC — Load test window (2 hours) — we recommend running heavy KV-cache + burst tests in this slot

If those blocks don't work, we can run a rotating cadence across three consecutive days to surface timing conflicts. Could you tell us:
1) Which of the three blocks your engineering team can definitely attend?
2) Any blackout windows (e.g., compliance reviews / town halls) next week?
3) Who from your side should receive the runbook and invites (I only have Samantha and Tom listed now)?

Attachments: 2027-05-18_BPA_POC_Agenda.pdf (pdf), POC_runbook_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks — looking forward to aligning.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@brightpath.ai>

Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: POC deep-dive sprint — proposed kickoff blocks and hands-on windows

Thanks, Marissa —

This looks good and the attachments are helpful. Quick notes from our side:
- Confirmed attendees: me (Samantha), Tom (platform), and Alex Chen (senior infra engineer, alex.chen@brightpath.ai). We'll add Alex to the invite if that's OK.
- Preferred blocks: Day 1 (US/EU overlap) is fine for leadership; Day 2 EU morning works best for our prompt team; Day 3 late US-PT is tricky for us because we have a release freeze starting that evening.
- Can we shift the load test window to earlier in the APAC morning (e.g., 09:30 APAC local) to avoid the release freeze? That would still be late EU but avoids the US-night conflict.

Blackouts: Friday 21st has a mandatory company-wide all-hands; avoid that date.

If you can propose a rotated alternative that keeps the prompt workshop in EU-morning and moves the load test to an APAC-friendly morning, we should be able to attend all three sessions across the team.

Appreciate it — Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Platform, BrightPath Analytics
Samantha@brightpath.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: POC deep-dive sprint — updated rotation proposal

Thanks for the context, Samantha — that helps. Alex, welcome — I've attached the runbook; feel free to flag anything that should change before invites go out.

New rotation (avoids BrightPath company all-hands on 21st and moves load test into APAC morning):
- Rotation A (Day 1): 16:00 US-ET / 21:00 EU — architecture review (45m) + routing sketches
- Rotation B (Day 2): 09:30 EU local / 17:30 APAC local — prompt workshop (60m) — preserves EU-morning preference
- Rotation C (Day 3): 09:30 APAC local / 18:30 EU (previous night for US) — load tests (2 hours) run primarily from APAC region to reduce customer disruption

Operational notes:
- Dev will own the load test runbook and will coordinate a short pre-flight check 24 hours prior.
- We'll send separate calendar invites with timezone-localized times; please confirm which timezone you prefer invites in (we can send in your local timezone or UTC).

Action items:
- Samantha: confirm Alex's inclusion and the APAC-morning load test slot (yes/no)
- Tom: share any infra ACLs or allowlist IPs we need ahead of load tests
- Alex: quick scan of runbook and reply with redlines before EOD Thursday (20 May)

I'll tentatively hold the slots in our calendar and circulate invites once we have confirmation.

—Marissa
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: POC deep-dive sprint — load test operational note

Quick operational note from my side:

If we're moving the heavy load window to APAC-morning (09:30 local), please confirm:
- Expected sustained concurrency (rps or concurrent sessions) so I can size batch knobs and KV-cache warmup; suggest we start at 100 rps and ramp to 500 rps over 20 minutes as a baseline.
- Allowlist: please add 35.197.65.132/32 and 34.120.1.10/32 to your temporary allowlist for the test agents, and ensure any egress NAT preserves TLS SNI for debugging.
- Pre-flight: I'll run a 15-minute prefix-cache warmup 30 minutes before the load window. That will cut cold-start tail latency during the ramp.

If that plan is OK I'll add the load curve to the runbook and include estimated token counts so you can approve any quota bumps.

Thanks — Dev
